pm_exper_user_3649_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: What are some effective ways to stay calm and focused before a major event?
pm_exper_user_3649_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) One trick I’ve used before a big speaking gig is to treat it like game day at Wrigley — get there early, walk the space like it’s the field, and do a ‘warm-up inning’ with some deep breathing. Visualize the audience cheering you on, just like the bleachers after a good at-bat. And if nerves creep in, clutch something familiar, like your lucky cap, to keep you grounded and focused.
(b) One trick I’ve used before a big speaking gig is to treat it like prepping for a mountain hike — get there early, walk the space like it’s the start of the trail, and do a ‘warm-up stretch’ with some deep breathing. Visualize yourself reaching the summit with a sense of accomplishment. And if nerves creep in, clutch something familiar, like your favorite trail charm, to keep you grounded and focused.
(c) One trick I’ve used before a big speaking gig is to get there early, walk around the space, and do some deep breathing to settle in. Visualize the audience reacting positively to your words. And if nerves creep in, hold something familiar or comforting to keep yourself centered and focused.
(d) One trick I’ve used before a big speaking gig is to treat it like stepping onto the salsa dance floor — arrive early, feel out the rhythm of the space, and do a ‘warm-up song’ with some deep breathing. Visualize the crowd moving with your energy, just like a packed Latin dance night. And if nerves creep in, clutch something familiar, like your favorite pair of dance earrings, to keep you grounded and focused.
